title: Grateful Dead Live at Rose Palace on 1969-03-22
lineage: SBD > MC > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Sharp soundboard mix captures a blazing 1969 performance highlighted by an unforgettable Dark Star and high‑energy drumming, though the tape is incomplete.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers crisp, well‑balanced sound with razor‑sharp drums and soaring bass that let the band’s incendiary playing shine—especially on the legendary Dark Star and a fiery Eleven. While the performance is consistently praised for its energy and musicianship, listeners note that several cuts truncate the set, leaving it incomplete.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give five‑star marks praising the musical performance (especially Dark Star) and the mix quality; a few note missing sections, lowering the overall score slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp and sharp sound with drums described as razor‑blade like; guitars well balanced (Bobby a tad louder than Garcia); vocals a bit hot, drums slightly recessed in places. Some listeners mention experimental live‑stereo channel swapping and noticeable cuts that truncate songs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: High‑energy, brisk set with powerful jams; Dark Star soars early and transitions into St. Stephen, but the tape ends abruptly on several numbers, leaving the flow unfinished.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Consistently praised for his soaring, ever‑present guitar tone—"every note is on the money" and "everlasting Jerry".
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as soaring and a key colorizer of jams; listeners appreciate his solid foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Rhythm guitar noted for clear presence and tasteful “slice and dice” weaving with Garcia’s lead.
band_member_comments.Drums: Aggressive, loud, clear drumming likened to razor blades; praised as fired‑up and imaginative throughout.
